This is a post for the people interested in the broader strategy of the Men's Rights movement.

It's pretty clear at this point that MRAs are involved in a very complicated, very long game where the establishment is hostile to them. It's not just a political problem; most political parties have problems from an MRA's perspective, and a lot of MRAs' difficulties stem from social norms that don't have purely political solutions. It's not just economic or educational, either. It's a game played simultaneously on a lot of different, interlocking domains.

Right now, MRAs' opponents are much more powerful, they're better coordinated, and they have tons more experience looking at the big picture and figuring out how they fit into it. Any attempt to reform society will have to engage in a multilayered effort that will be AT LEAST as complicated as the feminist movement in the 1970s-1990s.

Might I suggest a framework that toppled half a dozen dictatorships?

I don't know how many here have heard of him, but Gene Sharp's writings are the gold standard for nonviolent, multi-dimensional social campaigns. They're much more detailed than something like Alinsky's "Rules for Radicals", which focuses on tactics and short-term issues. Sharp, on the other hand, wrote encyclopedically about how to destabilize unfair institutions society-wide, and his methods turned out to be really good at it.

REALLY good.

Within the last couple decades, peaceful revolutions in Serbia, Kyrgyzstan, Ukraine, Georgia, and Belarus toppled dictatorships using Sharp as a model. The 2009 movement that freaked out the Iranian regime also used Sharp, although less successfully. Not to mention that the Egyptian Revolution that kicked out Mubarak was influenced by Sharp, as were more limited 2000's movements in Lebanon and Kuwait.

Did I mention that it's a DECENTRALIZED framework, specifically designed for movements that don't have massive institutional power or heavy organization?

Best of all, the nonviolent struggle think-tank that works on this stuff publishes all of its work for free. In 31 freaking languages. http://www.aeinstein.org/english/

A selection of the most relevant work. Have a read: http://www.aeinstein.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/198-Methods.pdf (a grab bag of tactics drawn from across the world) http://www.aeinstein.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/HNVSW-updated-Jan-2015.pdf http://www.aeinstein.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/FDTD.pdf http://www.aeinstein.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/09/OSNC.pdf The framework is also taught in game form, which was designed for activist training and classroom use. It's like a buck used on Amazon.

Hope this is useful.
